scenes.title: Festinger's 1954 Comparison Scale Meets the Olympic 1st / 2nd / 3rd Podium: Beaming Bronze (7.1) vs Disappointed Silver (4.8)!

layout.description: Sunlit high-key documentary studio stage featuring a crisp **white three-tier 1st / 2nd / 3rd Championship Podium** alongside Leon Festinger's **1954 Upward vs Downward Comparison Sightline Board** ('2nd Place Silver Looks UP at 1st -> 4.8 Joy | 3rd Place Bronze Looks DOWN at 4th -> 7.1 Joy!').

positions.who: Silver-Position Athlete mannequin (on #2 platform in white track tracksuit)
positions.where: gazing sideways and UPWARD at the higher #1 platform with folded arms and a tight, wistful expression (4.8/10)

positions.who: Bronze-Position Athlete mannequin (on #3 platform in matching white tracksuit)
positions.where: glancing DOWNWARD toward the empty #4 floor mat off the podium and throwing both arms up in an exuberant, beaming smile (7.1/10)!

positions.who: Leon Festinger / Researcher mannequin (in tailored blazer with clipboard)
positions.where: tracing the opposite visual comparison arrows from Tier #2->#1 (Upward Contrast) and Tier #3->#4 (Downward Relief) onto the 7.1 vs 4.8 rating chart

props.name: three-tier white 1st / 2nd / 3rd Podium + #4 Floor Marker
props.period_detail: stages the single most counterintuitive proof of Social Comparison ever filmed

props.name: Upward vs Downward Sightline Chart ('Silver 4.8 vs Bronze 7.1')
props.period_detail: visualizes Festinger's reference-point mechanics in one instant
props.physical_behavior: explains why better objective rank felt worse

actions.verb_sequence: turns head upward toward Tier #1 -> shoulders slump slightly knowing 0.05 seconds cost 1st place
looks down at the empty #4 floor mat -> beams wide raising both hands in celebration as Researcher logs 7.1 vs 4.8!

reactions.reaction: realize happiness followed the *comparison arrow*, not the objective stopwatch!

scenes.wardrobe: Clean classic white-and-navy Olympic track warmups; mid-century academic wool blazer and tie.
scenes.recognition_hook: Finish second in the entire world and sulk at 4.8; finish worse in third place and beam at 7.1 — because Silver looks up at 1st while Bronze looks down at 4th!

key_visual.description: a sunlit three-tier 1st-2nd-3rd podium with a #4 floor mat where the 3rd-place athlete celebrates joyfully looking toward 4th while the 2nd-place athlete looks wistfully up at 1st beside a 7.1-vs-4.8 chart

scenes.title: Hypothesis III: Why Your Classmate Stings & Federer Doesn't
scenes.era: 1954, University of Minnesota / Stanford seminar room

layout.description: Bright table showing a weekend tennis player unbothered by a World Champion poster while leaning intently over a next-door neighbor's club scorecard.

positions.where: mapping peak comparison intensity strictly inside the 'Close Similarity Zone'

props.name: Similarity Bell-Curve plaque ('Too Far = 0 Sting | Close Peer = Peak Comparison!')

actions.verb_sequence: ignores world-record poster -> leans closely over peer's nearly identical score

scenes.recognition_hook: You never lose a minute's sleep over an astronaut's trophy — Festinger's similarity detector only fires on people standing right next to your rung!

scenes.title: 150 Real Villagers vs 10,000 Curated Highlight Reels

layout.description: Contrast board showing 'Ancestral Village (150 Real Lives)' vs 'Infinite Feed (Top 0.01% Filtered Highlights)' draining mood.

positions.where: setting down an endless highlight-reel feed after spotting the artificial upward-comparison trap

props.name: 150 Real Lives vs 10,000 Highlight Reels board
props.period_detail: shows how modern feeds super-stimulate a 1954 evolutionary gauge

actions.verb_sequence: turns phone screen face-down and opens personal progress log

scenes.recognition_hook: Comparing your Tuesday bloopers against 10,000 strangers' once-a-year highlight reels rigs Festinger's ruler against you.

scenes.title: Switching to Temporal Comparison ('Me Today vs Me Last Spring')

layout.description: Warm desk holding a personal '6-Month Progress Graph' rising steadily upward with zero neighbor columns.

positions.where: plotting today's personal best against their own April baseline with genuine pride

props.name: Personal Temporal Progress Chart ('April -> July -> October')
props.period_detail: Lyubomirsky's habit of chronically happy high-achievers

actions.verb_sequence: marks new personal milestone -> smiles unbothered by outside noise

scenes.recognition_hook: Keep 100% of your drive and drop 90% of the sting by competing against who YOU were six months ago.
